resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy for sale (certificate of continued occupancy / zoning certificate of compliance)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Hasbrouck Heights Building Department (Construction and Code Enforcement); inspections by the Fire Chief
requirements: CO form from the Building Department, 320 Boulevard, with buyer and seller information including the buyer's phone number
Inspection done by the Heights Fire Chief (Rob Knobloch)

Zoning certificate of compliance on a change in ownership: the premises must conform to zoning (or a variance or lawful nonconforming use), meet Planning Board / Board of Adjustment conditions and the Property Maintenance Code
Owner-occupied single-family homes sold to an owner-occupant are reviewed only for zoning conformity

fees.label: Certificate of Occupancy for sale, one family
fees.quote: Fees are as follows: $50.00 for one family, $75.00 for two family.

fees.label: Certificate of Occupancy for sale, two family
fees.quote: Fees are as follows: $50.00 for one family, $75.00 for two family.

fees.label: Certificate of continued occupancy, single-family dwelling (Borough Code 133-12)
fees.quote: For a certificate of continued occupancy for a single-family dwelling, the sum of $50.

fees.label: Certificate of continued occupancy, two-family dwelling (Borough Code 133-12)
fees.quote: For a certificate of continued occupancy for a two-family dwelling, the sum of $75.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Get the residential CO form at the Building Department, 320 Boulevard, Hasbrouck Heights (Monday to Friday 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; summer hours 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.). Include buyer and seller information and the buyer's phone number, pay the fee, and allow two weeks. The Fire Chief does the inspection.

evidence.quote: Yes, we require a CO for the sale of a residential home as well as the sale of a commercial property.
The CO form for a residential home can be obtained at the Building Dept, 320 Boulevard.
Allow two weeks for processing. Rob Knobloch, Heights Fire Chief, does the inspections.

a zoning certificate of compliance shall be required for the continued occupancy of any premises or part thereof: upon every change of use from one classification under the Zoning Chapter to another classification; upon any change in occupancy; or upon any change in ownership of the subject premises.

resale_co.notes: The Building Department FAQ says a CO is required for the sale of a residential home, $50.00 one family and $75.00 two family, with inspections by Fire Chief Rob Knobloch (who is also the Fire Official). The Borough Code matches: Section 133-12A(11) sets certificate of continued occupancy fees of $50 (single-family) and $75 (two-family), and Section 275-39 requires a zoning certificate of compliance on any change in ownership, with the same $50 / $75 fees listed in Section 133-30C. It appears to be one certificate and one fee, but confirm that the zoning certificate and the CO are not billed separately. Ordinance text was read through a text reader of ecode360. Landlord registration (Chapter 212) is a rental program, not a resale requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area, and carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas, as required by N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 (no Borough checklist found online)
The Borough's sale CO inspection is done by the Fire Chief / Fire Official

authorities.name: Hasbrouck Heights Fire Prevention Bureau (Fire Department)
authorities.lead_time: Allow two weeks for the sale CO, which the Fire Chief inspects
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application or fee was found online. The Building Department's sale CO is inspected by the Fire Chief; call the Fire Prevention Bureau (201-288-4110) to confirm whether the smoke/CO certificate is issued with the CO or needs its own application.

evidence.quote: The local enforcing agency shall be the Fire Prevention Bureau of the Fire Department of the Borough of Hasbrouck Heights.
Allow two weeks for processing. Rob Knobloch, Heights Fire Chief, does the inspections.
LEAID: 0225-001 Enf Auth. Fire Dept Fire Official Robert Knobloch Phone (201) 288-4110 Addr: 210 Boulevard Hasbrouck Hgts NJ 07604 ... Email rknobloch@hasbrouck-heightsnj.org

fire_cert.notes: The Fire Prevention page lists the Bureau phone (201-288-4110), Fire Official Robert Knobloch and secretary Nancy Halloran, with office hours Monday through Friday 9 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. No separate smoke/CO certificate fee was found in the Borough Code (Chapter 139 adopts state permit fees; Chapter 133-15 covers other fire fees). Because the Fire Chief inspects for the sale CO, the smoke/CO check is likely part of that inspection, but this is not stated in writing. The email comes from the state fire directory.

other_items.label: Zoning certificate of compliance
other_items.detail: Borough Code Section 275-39 requires a zoning certificate of compliance on any change in ownership; fees in Section 133-30C are $50 (single-family) and $75 (two-family).

other_items.label: Open permit search
other_items.detail: To get a list of open or closed permits on a property, submit an OPRA request to the Borough Clerk; the response normally takes about 7 business days.

open_questions: Is the smoke/CO certificate issued as part of the Building Department sale CO, or is there a separate Fire Prevention application and fee?
Are the zoning certificate of compliance and the certificate of continued occupancy one combined $50 / $75 fee or two separate fees?
How long is the CO valid, and is there a reinspection fee?
